messages.subject: mapping species specific traits
parts:
Hello,
I am trying to map several species specific traits but I am having trouble because marker order is poorly conserved between species.  I using one of the two linkage maps to do the QTL mapping but I keep getting odd results.  For example I will get two additive markers that are only 2 cM apart.  I am assuming this is because of the problems with marker order.  Is there any way to fix this or should I just do ANOVA qtl mapping? 

Any help would be greatly greatly appreciated,
Emma

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapping species specific traits
parts: "I will get two additive markers that are only 2 cM apart. I am assuming this is because of the problems with marker order. Is there any way to fix this or should I just do ANOVA qtl mapping?"

You want to first correct problems in marker order if possible. Are there markers in-between those two inferred QTL? I would use effectplot() or plotPXG() to plot the genotypes at the two loci against the phenotype. Often a few outlying phenotypes will lead to inference of two QTL linked tightly in repulsion.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapping species specific traits
parts:
It looks quite interesting. The first thing I'd check is how many individuals are AA at c12m6 and AB at c12m10. Those recombinants are the ones showing the effect.

I like to look at plotPXG as well as effectplot, to see the individual phenotypes. Do something like:

plotPXG(mycross, marker=c("c12m6", "c12m10"))

karl
